definition: A visual organization test is a visuospatial assessment task used to examine how a person organizes and interprets visual information. In the source, an nTMS-based version of the Hooper Visual Organization Test was used during brain mapping to help identify cortical areas involved in the visuospatial network.

reasons: The packet supports that an nTMS-implemented version of the Hooper Visual Organization Test was used for hemispheric mapping to identify cortical areas in the visuospatial network, but it does not support the added claim that the test is used to examine how a person organizes and interprets visual information.
The definition goes beyond the source by presenting a general characterization of the test’s function that is not stated in the packet.

The first sentence claims that a “visual organization test” is a “visuospatial assessment task” examining “how a person organizes and interprets visual information.” This is not stated or supported anywhere in the provided packet.

The packet specifically describes use of an “nTMS-implemented version of the Hooper Visual Organization Test (HVOT)” during mapping; it does not support the broader, generic characterization of “visual organization test” as such an assessment task.

While the second sentence’s general idea about an nTMS-based HVOT used for brain mapping is supported (nTMS-implemented HVOT used to identify cortical areas in the visuospatial network), the definition as a whole is not defensible due to the unsupported first sentence.
